title: The Wolf of Ironhollow
premise: Felix Oyelaran has spent his life copying prayers in Ironhollow, a valley warded against magic where debt to the Temple of the Quiet Flame keeps him bound and invisible. When prayers in the valley start being answered—impossible, since magic cannot follow—the old gods stir, and Felix discovers his bloodline is the anchor holding the wards together. Dragged beyond the valley by a fugitive knight and a dragon-keeper's orphan, he learns King Aldric has been hollowed and worn as a vessel by a devouring god, and that the last dragon's dying fire is the only force that can burn the usurper out. Felix must choose between severing his bloodline to free himself forever—destroying the valley's protection—or binding himself to the fire to save both king and kingdom, ending with him crowned not as royalty but as the valley's first free warden, his debts burned, his found family at his side.
about_author: Kestrel Montrose is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing medieval prayer books before turning to fantasy. They write about debt, faith, and the families we build when the ones we're given fail us.

chapters.title: Ink and Ash
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Establishes Ironhollow's ward-silence, Felix's crushing temple debt, and his habit of copying prayers he doesn't believe in. When a widow's prayer for rain is answered overnight, Felix is the only scribe who notices the ink on her petition moved. Emotional beat: quiet dread beneath a life of careful invisibility.

chapters.title: The Answered Prayer
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. More miracles ripple through the valley—crops healing, a dead child breathing. The temple elders panic and order the records sealed. Felix secretly copies the anomalous prayers, and the ink burns his fingers. Emotional beat: the thrill and terror of being the one who sees what others won't.

chapters.title: A Knight at the Gate
chapters.summary: Ser Maren Vale, fugitive knight of the outer kingdom, breaches the valley's border half-dead, pursued by crown inquisitors. She carries a dragon-scale sealed with royal blood. Felix hides her in the scriptorium's undercroft. Emotional beat: first crack in Felix's shell—choosing to help a stranger at real cost.

chapters.title: What the Wards Remember
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. She reveals the truth: King Aldric stopped speaking in his own voice a year ago; the old gods are answering prayers because the wards are failing—and Felix's family founded them. The scale reacts to Felix's touch, flaring with heat. Emotional beat: Maren's guilt over the king she failed, mirrored against Felix's fear of mattering.

chapters.title: Debt of Blood
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The temple discovers Maren and names Felix a heretic, doubling his debt as punishment. His childhood friend Brother Osric betrays him to protect the temple—or so it seems. Felix flees with Maren through the ward-line, and crossing it, magic floods him painfully. Emotional beat: exile as both loss and liberation.

chapters.title: The Color of the World
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Beyond the valley: color, noise, magic in everything. Overwhelming and beautiful. They reach the dragon-keeper's ruined eyrie and meet Wren, an orphan raised by the dying last dragon, Emberfall. Wren is feral, distrustful, and instantly fixated on Felix's dragon-scale. Emotional beat: wonder shadowed by homesickness.

chapters.title: Emberfall's Bargain
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The ancient dragon, guttering toward death, speaks to Felix through Wren: his bloodline was the price of the valley's peace, and only dragon-fire can unmake what wears the king's crown. Emberfall will give her last flame—but only if Felix carries it, which will mark him forever. Emotional beat: Wren's terror of losing the only parent she's known.

chapters.title: Road of Relics
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The trio travels toward the capital, gathering allies among god-touched outcasts: a hedge-witch, a mute giant, a defrocked inquisitor. Found family begins to coalesce around campfires. Inquisitors shadow them. Emotional beat: the tentative, clumsy warmth of belonging.

chapters.title: The Hollow King
chapters.summary: Aldric's POV. Inside the palace, the king surfaces briefly beneath the thing wearing him, leaving coded messages in state documents. He is aware, drowning, and has been leaving a trail for anyone brave enough to follow. Emotional beat: horror and heartbreaking dignity—Aldric fighting from inside his own cage.

chapters.title: Inquisitor's Mercy
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. The inquisitors catch them; their leader is Osric, who left the valley not to betray Felix but to undermine the temple from within. A tense standoff ends in uneasy alliance. Maren confronts her failure at the king's hollowing. Emotional beat: betrayal reframed, trust rebuilt on broken ground.

chapters.title: The God Beneath the Crown
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. In the capital's undercity, they learn the usurper is Vhalor, a god the old pantheon imprisoned, wearing Aldric to rebuild its body from worship. The answered prayers in Ironhollow were Vhalor baiting Felix out. Emotional beat: the crushing realization that Felix's invisibility was someone else's design.

chapters.title: What We Owe the Dead
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Emberfall's fire gutters; the dragon spends her last strength teaching Wren the fire-song that can carry flame after death. Wren refuses to accept it. Emotional beat: grief rehearsed, love that can't be bargained with.

chapters.title: Palace of Whispers
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Infiltration of the palace via the scriptors' guild—Felix's scribe skills finally weaponized. He reaches Aldric's coded messages and decodes the king's plan: the hollowing ritual requires a blood-anchor, and Aldric has been protecting the identity of the last one. Emotional beat: Felix realizing the anchor is him, and that the king has been shielding a stranger.

chapters.title: The Mask Slips
chapters.summary: Aldric's POV. Vhalor discovers the king's coded trail and tightens its grip. Aldric's consciousness begins dissolving. In a final act of will, he burns his own memories to hide the ritual's weakness. Emotional beat: self-erasure as the ultimate sacrifice, identity spent like coin.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Gate
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. The temple, coerced by Vhalor's agents, offers to pardon Felix if he surrenders the dragon-scale. Osric is exposed as a double agent—this time genuinely turned. The party scatters; Wren is captured. Emotional beat: found family fractured at the worst moment.

chapters.title: Iron in the Blood
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Alone, hunted, Felix uncovers the final truth: the wards, the debt, the valley—all built by his ancestors to imprison Vhalor, with his bloodline as the lock. His whole life of servitude was a prison's maintenance. Emotional beat: rage transmuting into resolve—he will not be a lock; he will be a key.

chapters.title: The Fire-Song
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. In Vhalor's throne room, Wren sings the fire-song Emberfall taught her—and Emberfall's last flame answers from across the world, igniting in Wren's chest. The dragon dies singing; the child carries the fire. Emotional beat: devastating, triumphant inheritance.

chapters.title: Coronation of Ash
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The climax begins: Felix walks into the throne room under a scribe's disguise, offering himself as Vhalor's anchor. Vhalor accepts, beginning the binding—unaware Felix carries the counter-ritual in his own blood and Wren carries the fire. Emotional beat: terror worn like calm, the gambit staked.

chapters.title: Unbinding
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converging. Maren and Osric hold the gates; the outcast allies ignite the undercity's old god-shrines to distract Vhalor. Felix begins the unbinding as Vhalor tears at his mind with every sin and debt he's ever carried. Emotional beat: endurance—the price of survival paid in full view.

chapters.title: The Last Flame
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. At the ritual's peak, Wren's fire meets Felix's blood. Vhalor is burned out of Aldric—but the flame demands a vessel to contain it, and Felix chooses himself, binding the fire into his bloodline willingly rather than as a curse. Aldric wakes, weeping, mortal, free. Emotional beat: agency reclaimed; the same binding, chosen, transforms.

chapters.title: The Weight of Crowns
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Aftermath in the capital: Aldric, diminished and honest, begins repairing a kingdom that worshipped his captor. He offers Maren her honor back; she asks for a purpose instead. The found family stands in the ruins, uncertain but together. Emotional beat: exhaustion, tenderness, the strange quiet after war.

chapters.title: The Warden of Ironhollow
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix returns to the valley—not as a debtor but as its first freely chosen warden, the dragon-fire settled in his blood keeping the wards alive by consent rather than curse. The temple's debts are struck; Osric tends the scriptorium; Wren stays, learning to be a person, not a vessel. Emotional beat: belonging earned, home redefined—survival's price finally paid in something other than himself.
